# onceover

> A profiler for Polars DataFrames (Rust core, Python bindings). `onceover.profile(df)` returns a ranked, evidence-backed report of what is structurally interesting in a table: dependencies, identities, conditional rules, gaps, panel completeness, column views, and more. MIT license.

## Using the library

- [Agent brief](AGENTS.md): what the tool does, the quickstart, budget semantics, how to read a report, the hints API, and what empty or partial results mean.
- [Python API](python/onceover/__init__.py): thin wrapper over the Rust core for `profile(df, budget=..., detectors=..., hints=..., spec=...)`, `infer_spec(df)`, `profile_many({name: frame, ...})`, and `partition_scagnostics(df)`. The report offers `.to_brief(chars)` (dense schema strip + short `[f1]` handles), `.to_digest(chars, compact=..., include_schema=...)`, `.to_json(compact=..., max_chars=...)`, `.to_markdown()`, `.to_html()` (`html` extra), `.data` (dict), `.findings_frame()`, `.associations()`, `.finding(id_or_handle)`, `.select(category=, type=, column=, target=)`, `.diff(other)`, `.verify(df)`, `.rows(id_or_handle, df)`, `.to_checks()`, and `.save(path)`. `profile_many` returns a Rust-backed `MultiTableReport` (`.candidates`, `.overlaps`, `.coverage`, `.to_digest()`, `.to_json(max_chars=...)`, `.candidates_frame()`). An `onceover` console command profiles files directly: `onceover data.parquet --format brief`, `--digest 4000 --compact`, `--format json --compact`, `--format markdown|html`, and several files together for the multi-table report.
- [Report schema](docs/report-schema.md): the JSON report's fields, by schema version.
- [Report JSON Schema](docs/report-schema.json): the machine-readable contract for report `schema_version` 0.8, validated against live reports in the test suite.
- [Entity fingerprints](docs/book/methodology/entity_fingerprints.ipynb): compare entity mixes over categorical dimensions and pairs, with row counts or declared weights, and look for changes along an axis.
- [Detector selection](docs/book/usage/capabilities.ipynb): use `onceover.RECOMMENDED_DETECTORS` for the default IDs, supply your own `detectors` list, or select `onceover.ALL_DETECTORS` explicitly.
- [Partitioned scatterplot diagnostics](docs/book/usage/find_partitioned_shapes.ipynb): select `detectors=["partition_scagnostics"]` for held-out partition findings in a profile. Call `onceover.partition_scagnostics(df)` for explicit pairs, context columns, or metrics.
- [Reading a report](docs/reading-a-report.md): a worked walkthrough on a real table.
- [Capability manifest](docs/capability-manifest.json): detectors, the categories each produces, and what each requires — generated from the library itself by `scripts/capability_manifest.py`.

## Benchmarks

- [Benchmark corpus](benchmarks/corpus/README.md): registry-driven corpus of real tables with documented behavior (business, UCI, synthetic, CrossCat, anomaly, and GritBot packs), bundled with attribution where the license allows; expectations are checked on every run.
- [Benchmark write-ups](docs/benchmarks/): protocol, results, and case dispositions for every recorded run. Project convention: a benchmark that is not in the docs does not exist.

## For agents working in this repo

- [Agent guide](docs/agents.md): build/test commands, conventions (executed notebooks, benchmark docs entries, the data license gate), and where things live.
